discussionThreads.author: cpmpml
discussionThreads.reason: Prior verified public staff explanation re-read; latest acknowledgment read, without independent measurement of the billing claim.
discussionThreads.summary: Kaggle Staff member Dustin says dataset download time does not count toward submission runtime. He explains that the live interactive quota display is an estimate and final usage corrects to container runtime when the session stops; data added while a container is running consumes quota. The staff explanation is publicly readable. Expanded CPMP acknowledgment says he had not checked the final adjustment and assumes staff is right; this is not independent confirmation.
discussionThreads.title: Are datasets download time include din submission sunning time?

discussionThreads.author: atelierzoe
discussionThreads.reason: Expanded mikelou1 branch read in Chrome and independently while logged out; public visibility established.
discussionThreads.summary: mikelou1 reports a score of 66% (about 60% local validation) in an expanded reply. Earlier replies deny using an NVARC ensemble and describe a kernel issue behind a lower result. The exact Qwen model variant and full recipe remain undisclosed. The current board independently shows the same entry at 66.39 and rank 13; the comment does not prove which change caused that gain.
discussionThreads.title: Qwen3.8-27B / Flash-Next: ARC-AGI-2 results within Kaggle’s compute limits?

discussionThreads.author: herbison
discussionThreads.reason: New Kaggle staff queue estimate verified in signed-in Chrome and logged-out public view.
discussionThreads.summary: In an October 16 reply, Kaggle staff member Dustin says ARC-2 queue delay has fallen to about three to five hours and most waiting is now actual submission runtime. He estimates turnaround below a day. Later participants still ask about long saves and runs; the staff estimate is dated, not a live service guarantee.
discussionThreads.title: Update on "Kaggle Error" Submissions & Queue Delays

discussionThreads.author: anlthms
discussionThreads.reason: Earlier lead re-read without login; body and visible replies publicly accessible. Preserve attribution and distinguish participant results from predictions.
discussionThreads.summary: Anil Thomas posts a prediction that nvbanana is likely to win and attributes his underlying data to huikang’s historical ARC-2 leaderboard page. CPMP replies that he does not know whether they will win, but their submissions have run fast so far. The prediction and response are contestant statements, not an organizer decision, verified winning forecast or disclosed current recipe. Exact root and reply times come from source tooltips.
discussionThreads.title: Pareto front says nvbanana is likely to win

discussionThreads.author: dmitriigluzdov
discussionThreads.reason: Earlier lead re-read without login; body and visible replies publicly accessible. Preserve attribution and distinguish participant results from predictions.
discussionThreads.summary: Dmitrii Gluzdov reports synthetic ARC-rule fine-tuning improves performance on unseen generated rules but has not shown a leaderboard gain. The current post describes 1,369 executable rules and 41,070 generated puzzles, two training approaches, and reported public scores of 30.83 for base NVARC, 29.03 for early LoRA, 27.92 for full LoRA and 29.17 for added blocks. He reports rerun variation of roughly two to four points. Training only on the hard-example file remains untried. These are the author’s experiments and noise estimate; augmented examples are not independent puzzles.
discussionThreads.title: Tried fine-tuning NVARC on new synthetic ARC tasks

discussionThreads.author: darrenamadeusmartin
discussionThreads.reason: Substantive source read and original replies checked; distinguish participant claims from organizer decisions. Logged-out access confirmed.
discussionThreads.summary: Darren Amadeus Martin proposes a deadline extension or GPU change because of grading delays. CPMP argues that a late GPU change would be unfair to teams that spent months tuning for 4xL4. The author replies that fixing the queue is preferable if possible and describes the hardware change as a contingent proposal. No organizer approval was seen.
discussionThreads.title: Petition to delay the end of competition and compute change

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize reports verified Reflection Beam 1.0 scores: ARC-AGI-2 23.5% at $0.61/task and ARC-AGI-1 74.0% at $0.31/task. Best scores use xhigh reasoning; high reaches 20.0% on ARC-AGI-2 at about 43% lower cost.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: New official model evaluation. Linked result page independently read in Chrome: semi-private best scores match. This is benchmark evaluation, not a Kaggle team score.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize places Argon behind Astra’s 99.9% ARC-AGI-3 result. It reports 62% fewer actions than the human baseline on the 25 public games, matching or beating three speedrun records and coming within 10% on six others.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Keep the public-demo action comparison separate from the semi-private Verified score.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize says API issues prevented complete standard-harness testing: low reasoning completed 42/55 games for 49.8%; medium completed 46/55 for 46.3%; high completed 19/55 and no score was published. Reported scores retain partial credit across all 55 games. Provider adapter preserves opaque reasoning and permits automatic compaction; standard harness carries notes between turns. Costs use introductory $2 input/$10 output per million tokens.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Material limit on harness comparisons. Do not present incomplete standard-harness runs as a clean capability ceiling.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announces Gemini 4 Argon Verified results: ARC-AGI-3 97.5% at $4.8K with the provider adapter and 49.8% at $5.8K with the standard harness; ARC-AGI-2 91.3% at $0.32/task and ARC-AGI-1 98.5% at $0.16/task. It calls Google DeepMind the second frontier lab above 95% on ARC-AGI-3.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Consequential organizer result. Separate from Kaggle standings. Standard-harness API incompletion is essential context; primary results introduction says 91.2% on v2 while its table and announcement say 91.3%.

socialPosts.author: 82deutschmark
socialPosts.summary: Mark Barney publicly welcomes Jack Cole to his ARC-AGI-2 team, using a Professor X metaphor, and states an ambition to reach gold. The post has ARC Mutants artwork. The announcement explicitly concerns ARC2; it does not add Cole to ARC3 Team Turducken.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Fresh public first-person confirmation supporting the commissioned ARC Mutants dispatch. Gold is an ambition, not an awarded medal.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize says Beam costs use Baseten pricing of $1.30 input and $4.30 output per million tokens. ARC-AGI-3 results are pending.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Keeps the cost basis and absence of ARC-AGI-3 results explicit.

dispatches.editorNote: Commissioned by Mark Barney, a member of ARC Mutants and the Digest’s head human editor. ARC Mutants competes in ARC2; Team Turducken is the separate ARC3 team.
dispatches.headline: Breaking afternoon edition: Jack Cole joins ARC Mutants for the ARC2 gold chase

image.alt: ARC Mutants at a glowing digital university filled with ARC grids: Mark with GPU gauntlets on the left, Jack Cole as the seated central mentor, Son at the front right, and an original helmeted character representing Ronen behind him.
image.caption: AI-generated editorial artwork approved by Mark Barney: ARC Mutants’ digital academy, created for ARC-AGI-2. Characters and equipment are fantasy; Ronen’s helmeted character is not a verified likeness.

sections.heading: Jack Cole joins the ARC2 squad
sections.text: Jack Cole has joined Mark Barney, Son Pham and Ronen in the ARC-AGI-2 competition. The team now appears on the public board as ARC Mutants, with the four accounts jcole75, markbarney, scizical and sonphamorg listed together. Mark confirmed the move to the Digest and commissioned this special afternoon announcement.

sections.heading: Two competitions. Two separate teams.
sections.text: ARC Mutants is the ARC2 entry, team 17023174. Team Turducken is the separate ARC3 entry, team 15605182. The teams share some people, but their competition entries, rosters and results are distinct. Jack’s arrival is an ARC2 announcement: he is not listed on Team Turducken’s ARC3 roster. The same ARC3 snapshot continues to list his jcole75 account with Abstraction Lab & MindsAI. Earlier ARC2 reports used Team Turducken for the entry now called ARC Mutants; that history must not be confused with the separate ARC3 team.

sections.heading: “Our own Professor X”
sections.text: “We’ve acquired our own Professor X and are honored to have Jack Cole join us,” Mark said. He called Cole “a true legend of ARC.” The welcome gives ARC Mutants its digital-academy theme: Cole as the cerebral mentor, Mark with his extravagant GPU rig, and Son and Ronen alongside them among glowing ARC grids. It is an affectionate team cartoon, not a claim about anyone’s role, equipment or powers.

sections.heading: A long ARC record comes with him
sections.text: Cole’s reputation has substance behind it. ARC Prize’s 2024 report credits MindsAI with the highest score, while noting that its closed-source submission was not eligible for a prize. The 2025 results place MindsAI third and give an honorable mention to Cole and Mohamed Osman’s paper, “Don’t throw the baby out with the bathwater: How and why deep learning for ARC.” These are earlier achievements, not this season’s results.

sections.heading: The ambition is gold
sections.text: “We’re hoping that our combined efforts in ARC2 can take us to gold,” Mark said. That is the new squad’s ambition, not a medal claim or a prediction. The news today is a confirmed teammate and a new ARC2 identity: Jack Cole joins ARC Mutants, while Team Turducken continues as the separate ARC3 team. Disclosure: Mark is both a competitor and the Digest’s head human editor; the welcome above is attributed to him.
